children: has launched a major reverse circulation and diamond drilling campaign at its Neds Creek copper project in Western Australia, targeting extensions to known mineralisation at the Ricci Lee, Thaduna, and Rooneys prospects.

The 19,500-metre campaign will comprise 21 holes for 9,572m to test the scale and depth potential of the high-grade Main Lode at Ricci Lee to approximately 600m depth, along with six holes for 4,119m to test down-plunge extensions to the Thaduna resource and 36 holes for 5,760m to test more than 500m of strike at the Rooneys structure.

Maiden drilling earlier this year delivered high-grade copper hits at Ricci Lee, substantially expanded the interpreted mineralised trend at Rooneys, and identified additional copper mineralisation across several regional targets.

Exploration of the Thaduna and Green Dragon deposits — which have a combined resource estimate of 5.3 million tonnes grading 2.3% copper for 121,000 tonnes of contained copper — has also advanced the company’s understanding of the broader potential at Neds Creek.
The new campaign will continue into the first half of next year, supported by a recent $9.2 million capital raising that saw the issue of approximately 88 million BOA shares priced at $0.105 each.

Maiden drilling at Ricci Lee defined an interpreted north-plunging high-grade shoot within the Main Lode, with select intersections of 22m at 3.05% copper from 250m including 9m at 6.86%, and 23m at 2.65% copper from 173m including 6m at 6.91%.

Thaduna was drilled to approximately 600m with only sparse exploration at depth, and historical holes at the base of the deposit returned best copper intersections of 7.5m at 8.25% copper from 572m including 6.15m at 9.94%, as well as 10.28m at 4.73% copper from 612m.

Previous aircore work at Rooneys extended the interpreted trend to more than 500m of strike and identified copper in new mineralised structures with assay highlights of 4m at 3.54% copper from 10m, 16m at 2.47% copper from 58m, and 10m at 1.75% copper from 51m.
Maiden high-grade results were also received from drilling at the Ward, Blockley, and Mueller prospects, highlighting the broader exploration potential at Neds Creek.
Managing director Graeme Purcell hoped the major campaign would build on maiden results that exceeded the company’s expectations and reinforced its confidence in Neds Creek’s copper potential.
“What is particularly encouraging is that we are seeing high-grade copper mineralisation across multiple prospects within a vast project area, which remains largely underexplored,” he said.

“We have wasted no time commencing our next phase of drilling—our immediate focus is on testing the depth and scale potential of Ricci Lee, extending the existing Thaduna resource, and following up the expanded mineralisation at Rooneys.”
“With a strong funding position, we believe we are well positioned to build on the achievements of this year and advance our strategy of growing the copper inventory at Neds Creek.”

title: BOA Resources Launches Major Drilling Campaign at Neds Creek Copper Project
